_comment: Roadmap-estate ratchet (road-to-estate-drawdown T2 + T3). POLICY ONLY — this file no longer stores a number. Until ADR-243 it carried a measured `baseline` object plus a `baseline_history` audit trail (113 entries at removal, last measurement 23/59/60), and that made it the most-conflicted non-generated path in the repository: 7 of 7 CONFLICTING open PRs on 2026-08-21, and 39 of 43 non-merge commits in a 60-day window moving the baseline. `check_estate_count` now MEASURES the floor on the base ref's own tree with the same functions it measures HEAD with, so the 'before' side is still something the change under review cannot rewrite — it is just no longer something a human has to remember to walk. Two failure classes went with the storage and are now unrepresentable: a baseline left above the truth (spendable headroom, which the gate used to fail on as an un-walked tightening), and a baseline left below it after main archived a roadmap without walking the number, which reddened every branch that merged main. The legitimate-growth path the stored number provided — a raise carrying a recorded reason — is replaced by `estate_growth_exempt: <reason>` in the frontmatter of a roadmap the change touches, read from the diff so it cannot be banked. T1's proposed ceilings stay under `target` and are still NOT registered: they are the maintainer's to set.

metric.basis: src/scripts/check_estate_count.ts. The live side uses collect() from update_roadmap_progress — the same parser the dashboard is generated from, imported rather than re-implemented. The floor side runs the SAME functions over a scratch copy of the base ref's agents/roadmaps/, materialised by _lib/base_tree.ts (git ls-tree + git cat-file --batch; `git archive` cannot be used here because .gitattributes carries `/agents export-ignore` and would yield an empty, silently-zero tree). SKILL METRICS (added 2026-08-24): _lib/skill_estate.ts walks src/skills/*/SKILL.md under the SAME root, so the floor side measures the base ref's own skill tree with the same function. That needs a SECOND materialised subtree — materialiseSubtree takes one prefix — and the two are independent on purpose: a base ref with no src/skills (an old tag, a shallow clone) drops the skill metrics and leaves the roadmap metrics ratcheting.
metric.active_roadmaps: non-draft roadmap candidates at the top level of agents/roadmaps/, as collect() counts them. This is exactly the number the dashboard header prints as 'N open roadmaps'.
metric.later_roadmaps: roadmap-shaped *.md files under agents/roadmaps/later/ — the same is_roadmap_candidate name filter the active side uses, so later/README.md is not counted. Counted from the filesystem because parked roadmaps sit outside collect()'s corpus by design; they are estate all the same, and a drawdown that moved everything into later/ and called the number down would be the burial T1's quality anchor exists to prevent.
metric.open_blockers: blockers whose Status does not start with `resolved`, summed over the active and later corpora.
metric.floor: the same three metrics measured at the base ref (origin/main, else the merge commit's first parent). No base ref resolves -> no floor -> the gate FAILS rather than skipping: a shrink-only gate with no floor passes every possible tree. `--base <ref>` is the explicit escape.
metric.skill_count: Maintained src/skills/*/SKILL.md files; `lifecycle: deprecated` EXCLUDED. The exclusion is load-bearing rather than tidy: with deprecated skills counted, deprecating one would create no headroom and the retirement mechanism would be unusable against its own gate. 0 skills carry it today, so the exclusion is a no-op now and a correctness property once a tranche lands. Measured 2026-08-24: 299. Reproduce with `find src/skills -name SKILL.md | wc -l` (299 including any deprecated) or `npx tsx -e "import {measureSkillEstate} from './src/scripts/_lib/skill_estate.ts'; console.log(measureSkillEstate(process.cwd()))"` for the split.
metric.skill_description_tokens: Exact-BPE tokens (js-tiktoken, cl100k_base, via _lib/token_count.ts gpt_tokens) across those skills' `description:` frontmatter fields ONLY — not bodies. Measured 2026-08-24: 11,461 over 299 skills (52,983 chars). A SECOND DIMENSION, not a companion figure: a count ratchet alone is gameable by merging four large skills into one file, which lowers the count while the description payload a host must carry stays put. AI council 2/2 (2026-08-24) asked for both in one gate over the roadmap's own recommendation of count-plus-informational-figure. UNRESOLVED rather than approximated: when the tokeniser does not resolve on either side the metric is dropped from the compare with a printed reason, because an exact reading against a proxy one differs by more than the growth this gate is trying to catch.
metric.skill_metric_rejected_candidates: Measured before choosing, not argued. (b) catalogue bytes via _lib/skill_catalogue.ts read 0 on a real checkout: readProjectedCatalogue walks .claude/skills, empty in any tree where `task generate-tools` cannot complete (it fails under projection.mode=scoped without the config package) — a ratchet whose reading depends on whether a generator ran reds for the environment. (d) host-listing slots are the host's decision, not the repository's: a measured install published its own budget event stating it had stripped every description and dropped 402 entries. Neither is reproducible from the repo, so neither can carry a floor.
metric.concern_count: Hook concerns declared under the `concerns:` map in src/scripts/hook_manifest.yaml. Measured 2026-08-30: 55. Reproduce with `npx tsx -e "import {countConcerns} from './src/scripts/_lib/concern_estate.ts';import fs from 'node:fs';console.log(countConcerns(fs.readFileSync('src/scripts/hook_manifest.yaml','utf-8')))"`. THE ORIGINATING ROADMAP'S REPRODUCE COMMAND IS A PROXY AND OVER-COUNTS, and the correction is recorded here rather than only in the roadmap because this file is what a later reader checks the number against. `grep -cE '^  [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*:$'` greps the WHOLE manifest, so it also counts members of `roles:`, `platforms:` and `native_event_aliases:`, which sit at the same two-space indent. Re-measured at the roadmap's own six pins the over-count is EXACTLY 16 every time: 63/65/65/68/69/71 by the grep is 47/49/49/52/53/55 scoped. Both consequences, because they point in opposite directions -- the FINDING survives untouched (the delta is constant, so the axis climbs +8 either way and is growing exactly as the roadmap says), and the ABSOLUTE FIGURE does not (the axis stands at 55, and a floor of 71 is one this gate's own parser could never reproduce, i.e. a gate that fails on its first honest run). REJECTED CANDIDATES, measured rather than argued: counting `platforms:` rows instead -- rejected, it is 8 and flat across all six pins, so it measures host coverage and not concern growth; counting the per-(platform,event) cap in lint_hook_concern_budget.ts -- rejected, DEFAULT_MAX_PER_EVENT=8 is blind to total growth by construction (eight new concerns spread across eight events violate nothing) and it ships DEFAULT_HARD_FAIL=false, which is why this axis needed a ratchet at all.

growth_allowances._comment: An exact floor leaves no incidental headroom, so every legitimate increase needs a named path. Two are automatic because existing policy already sanctions the act; the third is the general authorisation.
growth_allowances.active_roadmaps: +1 per addition carrying `estate_offset_exempt: <reason>` in its own frontmatter (unchanged T3 key). Without this the sanctioned un-offsettable addition would fail the count half with no green path.
growth_allowances.later_roadmaps: +1 per roadmap moved from the active top level into later/ in the same change. Parking relocates estate rather than creating it. It does NOT cover a later/ file that appears from nowhere, and it is keyed on parking rather than on any offset so that an archive move cannot buy a new later/ file.
growth_allowances.open_blockers: none. Nothing in the policy sanctions a new blocker, so it takes the claim path or nothing.
growth_allowances.claim: `estate_growth_exempt: <reason>` added, in this change, to the frontmatter of any roadmap under agents/roadmaps/. Authorises growth in any metric, with the reason printed. Diff-scoped, so a claim left in a file authorises nothing later — the banking failure a stored baseline had. Deliberately unbounded, which a stored baseline could not afford: there the surplus of an over-raise was inherited by the next change, where nobody could act on it; here the next change's floor IS this change's measurement, so there is no surplus to inherit.
growth_allowances.skill_count: 0 — no allowance, deliberately. The defect this metric addresses is a corpus that grew +8 in one release (290 at 14.0.0, 291 at 14.9.0 and 14.10.0, 299 at 14.11.0) with nothing objecting. An addition takes the estate_growth_exempt claim path — a recorded reason read from the diff — or it fails.
growth_allowances.skill_description_tokens: 0 — same reasoning. An addition that grows the description payload without adding a file is the gaming path this dimension exists to close, and an allowance would reopen it.
growth_allowances.concern_count: 0 — no allowance, deliberately, and the same reason skill_count gives. An allowance reopens the gaming path the dimension exists to close. Sharper here than for skills: eight concerns spread across eight events violate the existing per-event cap zero times, which is precisely why a total-growth ratchet was needed and precisely why it must not carry a per-change freebie. An addition takes the estate_growth_exempt claim path — a recorded reason read from the diff — or it fails.

target._comment: T1's proposed ceilings, kept as the destination. PROPOSALS, NOT REGISTERED: the roadmap says in as many words that both numbers and the window belong to the maintainer, and no date is pinned in this file. Nothing reads these values — `one_in_one_out.applies_above_active` is the only threshold the gate evaluates.
target.window: roughly six weeks from campaign start (drafted; unregistered)

one_in_one_out._comment: T3. `applies_above_active: null` means UNCONDITIONAL. T3 phrases the condition as 'while the active count sits above target', and T1 says the target belongs to the maintainer — so rather than inventing a ceiling so the condition could be evaluated, null states that no ceiling is registered and the lint therefore applies. Registering a number here is how it gets a threshold; registering one above the live count is how it is turned off.
one_in_one_out.exemption: estate_offset_exempt: <reason> in the added roadmap's own frontmatter. The key lives in the file rather than in this config for the reason RATCHET_RESET_KEY gives for living inside its baseline JSON: the claim shows up in the diff of the change that makes it.
